concepts.def: One of 88 official regions of the sky defined by the IAU, each containing a recognised star pattern used to navigate the night sky by eye.
A familiar pattern of stars that is not an official constellation, such as the Plough within Ursa Major or the Summer Triangle spanning three constellations.
A measure of how bright an object looks from Earth, where smaller numbers are brighter; the naked eye reaches about magnitude 6 in dark skies.
The apparent daily east-to-west movement of stars across the sky, caused by the Earth's rotation on its axis from west to east.
A star close enough to the celestial pole that it never sets for a given observer, instead circling the pole above the horizon all night.
The band of constellations along the ecliptic through which the Sun, Moon and planets appear to move as seen from Earth.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Naked-Eye Astronomy — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Naked-Eye Astronomy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Naked-Eye Astronomy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: On the magnitude scale, a brighter star has a:
options: Larger number
Smaller (or even negative) number
Number of exactly zero
Letter rather than a number

mcqs.q: The Plough is best described as:
options: A constellation
An asterism
A planet
A galaxy

mcqs.q: The nightly east-to-west motion of the stars is caused by:
options: The stars orbiting Earth
The Earth's rotation
The Sun's gravity
The Moon's pull

mcqs.q: A circumpolar star is one that:
options: Never rises
Never sets for that observer
Is always directly overhead
Is actually a planet

mcqs.q: Does a higher magnitude number mean a brighter star?
options: No - smaller and even negative numbers are brighter on the magnitude scale.
Yes, a bigger number means brighter.
Because the sky is a solid moving dome.
Magnitude measures distance, not brightness.

mcqs.q: Why do stars appear to move across the sky at night?
options: Because the sky is a solid moving dome.
Because the stars physically orbit the Earth each night.
Magnitude measures distance, not brightness.
Because the Earth rotates on its axis.
No - it is an asterism within the constellation Ursa Major.
Because the sky is a solid moving dome.
Yes, it is its own constellation.
It is a small nearby galaxy.
